report:
**Conclusion: Your view is correct — the claim that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19 is false.**

**Evidence supporting this conclusion:**

1. **World Health Organization (WHO):** The WHO explicitly listed garlic among its COVID-19 "mythbusters," stating there is no evidence that eating garlic protects against or cures COVID-19. They noted there was no licensed medication to cure COVID-19 at the time the claim spread. ([WHO Mythbusters](https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters))

2. **Multiple fact-checking organizations:** AFP Fact Check, FactCheck.org, Africa Check, Rappler, and India's PIB Fact Check all independently debunked the viral social media claim that "one bowl of freshly boiled garlic water" cures the novel coronavirus. The claim originated as an anonymous chain message and had no medical backing. ([AFP Fact Check](https://factcheck.afp.com/health-experts-refute-false-claims-drinking-boiled-garlic-water-cures-novel-coronavirus); [FactCheck.org](https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/); [Africa Check](https://africacheck.org/fact-checks/meta-programme-fact-checks/no-garlic-doesnt-cure-coronavirus-get-covid-19-facts-only))

3. **What the science actually says:** Garlic does contain compounds like allicin with demonstrated *in vitro* antimicrobial and antiviral properties, and one review noted garlic's potential as a functional food for immune support. However, laboratory activity in a petri dish does not translate to curing a viral infection in humans. No clinical trial has shown garlic or garlic water cures COVID-19. ([PMC review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7434784/))

4. **AAP FactCheck** also addressed a later variant of the claim, noting that an in-vitro study testing garlic extract against COVID-19 did not prove it could cure the virus in humans. ([AAP FactCheck](https://www.aap.com.au/factcheck/garlic-covid-cure-claim-crushed-by-experts/))

**Bottom line:** While garlic has general health benefits and some antimicrobial properties, there is no scientific or clinical evidence that boiled garlic water cures COVID-19. The claim is a well-documented piece of pandemic misinformation.
